A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of methylphenidate on hyperactivity in 5-day old 6-hydroxodopamine lesioned rats is mediated by the noradrenergics system and not the dopaminergic system.
the effects of the stimulants on hyperactivity are not due to their action on dopamine, but are due to their effects on norepinephine and serotonin.

6-OH-DA lesioning in rats is a useful model for studying the pathophysiology of ADHD and that the behavioral effects of the selective DA transporter inhibitors in the lesioned rats are consistent with their clinical actions in humans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
drugs which increase activity of the NE or 5-hydroxy-tryptamine (serotonin) system may be effective in the treatment of ADHD.
the behavioral effects of methylphenidate are mediated by release of serotonin, and not dopamine, and that the effects of amphetamine are mediated by release both of dopamine and serotonin.
